_readme: Hand-maintained. Edit this file directly in the repo whenever a real event happens (BOJ decision, new budget, confirmed intervention, election/fiscal news). Everything here is tagged tier='event-driven' on the frontend — it is correct-as-of its own date, not daily-live, because the underlying real-world thing itself doesn't change daily.

boj_policy_rate.context: Held at 1.00% on an 8-1 vote (Takata dissented, proposed 1.25%). Hiked from 0.75% to 1.00% in June 2026. Ueda flagged possible move as early as September/October. Update 2026-08-13: BOJ's Summary of Opinions from the July meeting flagged growing inflation risk, with one board member suggesting the pace of hikes could accelerate.

kokusaihi_breakdown.note: 利払費(interest) vs 債務償還費(principal redemption, rolled over via new issuance) — these are NOT the same burden. Use interest_only for a true sustainability read.

debt_service_ratio.context: Interest-only ratio (15.6%) sits in Normal zone. Gross kokusaihi-to-revenue (37.4%) sits in Danger zone by the >30% threshold — the two tell different stories, which is why both are shown rather than collapsed into one number.
debt_service_ratio.source: Japan MOF FY2026 budget documents, Dec 2025 / Feb 2026

intervention_log.type: Coordinated US-Japan intervention — first joint operation in ~30 years
intervention_log.mechanism: Unusual funding: NY Fed sold EUROS (not USD) to buy JPY, via Goldman Sachs/Morgan Stanley, per FT. Treasury Sec. Bessent confirmed on 2026-08-03. A trader's notepad photographed at Camp David read 'Buy JPY $5-10bn'.
intervention_log.why_it_matters: Analysts (Setser/CFR, Brooks/Brookings) read this as more about protecting the UST market than the yen itself — funding via EUR avoids forcing Japan to sell Treasuries to raise USD, which would have pushed UST yields up. This is the US actively managing the 'Japan capital repatriation -> UST selling' tail risk from the carry-trade chain.
intervention_log.confidence: confirmed by Treasury Secretary, amounts not officially disclosed
intervention_log.source: CFR / CNBC / FT / Axios / OMFIF, 2026-08-01 to 2026-08-07

intervention_log.confidence: estimate — inferred from BOJ account data, not officially confirmed by MOF (official quarterly breakdown lags ~3 months)

fiscal_political_calendar.note: Primary driver of the 2026 JGB long-end selloff — a fiscal/political story more than a pure BOJ-normalization story.

fiscal_political_calendar.event: Snap election called, consumption tax cut on food pledged
fiscal_political_calendar.note: 30Y JGB jumped 42bp in two sessions on this announcement.
Bond issuance held flat vs plan — a deliberate signal to bond markets.

fiscal_political_calendar.event: Bessent confirms coordinated intervention; calls for FIMA repo facility expansion
fiscal_political_calendar.note: Bessent publicly said intervention 'can send a market signal, but Japan also needs to deliver policies that support the currency' — i.e. the US framed this as buying time, not a fix. Japan's FinMin said future dollar-raising would prioritize the FIMA repo facility (borrow USD against JGB collateral) over selling Treasuries outright.

fiscal_political_calendar.event: Intervention effect fades — USDJPY retraces ~half the move
fiscal_political_calendar.note: USDJPY at ~159.4 (Aug 14 close), down ~1% on the week, having given back roughly half of the late-July/early-Aug intervention gain with no follow-up intervention. OMFIF's read: yen weakness is now openly a political issue domestically (real incomes, inflation), and intervention 'checks the box on being seen as doing something' rather than fixing the underlying rate differential.

risk_thresholds.note: These are Josh's own risk bands from the Japan Macro Crisis Map analysis, not universal constants — shown so the frontend can flag when a live-api reading crosses into Watch/Danger.

jgb_40y.danger: >4.5% — insurers become forced sellers at this line, mechanical not sentiment-driven

debt_service_gross_ratio.note: no separate band defined yet — currently reads as Danger under the same >30% line, flagged as a methodology question, not a confirmed verdict

ust_30y.danger: >5.5% — highest since 2001 territory, already close as of Aug 2026

vix.danger: >30 — but watch this TOGETHER with Valuation Heat, a low VIX during high Valuation Heat is itself the warning, not just a high VIX alone

buffett_indicator.note: methodology changed 2026-08 (Wilshire 5000 source discontinued by FRED in 2024, switched to Fed Z.1 nonfinancial-corporate-equities/GDP). Not enough history on the new series yet to set a real band — treat the number directionally only until we've watched it for a few months. Do not apply the old 235%-era intuition to this new number.

unemployment.note: Sahm Rule, not a fixed level: Danger triggers when unemployment rate rises >=0.5 percentage points above its own trailing-12-month low. This needs the 12-month-low value tracked alongside the current rate to auto-flag — not yet wired up, treat manually for now.

dxy.danger: >105 — dollar squeeze stresses global carry trades and EM/JPY funding

us_hy_credit_spread.danger: >5% — real credit-market stress, tends to show up before equity vol does

wti_oil.danger: >100 — energy-shock inflation risk, directly feeds Japan's import-price channel
wti_oil.note: this band only covers the high side (inflation-shock risk). A fast drop below ~$50 is a different signal — demand-destruction/recession — not captured by this band.

rrp.note: No fixed danger level — what matters is the TREND. RRP near-zero (parked cash mostly drained) means less spare liquidity cushion in the system; a level under ~$50bn after being much higher is the thing to watch, not a specific number.

ust_2s10s.note: Danger isn't a level, it's the SIGN: negative (inverted, short rates above long rates) has preceded most US recessions historically, though with a long and variable lag (often 12-24 months). A positive-but-narrowing spread deserves attention too.

oat_bund_spread.danger: >100bp — French fiscal/political premium becoming systemic; ECB backstop (TPI) becomes the debate

btp_bund_spread.danger: >250bp — 2022 stress area; 2011-12 euro crisis peaked far higher

uk_10y.danger: >5.5% — gilt-market stress zone (Oct-2022 LDI episode context); fiscal-credibility risk

fx_cny.danger: >5% depreciation in 3M — managed currency, so a fast move implies policy stress

fx_mxn.danger: >8% in 3M — EM risk-off / US policy shock

em_corp_oas.danger: >5% — EM credit stress; 2020 peak was far higher

em_stress_score.danger: >=4 of 7 flags — broad EM stress, not an idiosyncratic one

nfci.danger: >0.5 — financial conditions clearly tighter than average (0 = long-run average)

jobless_claims.danger: >320k sustained — labour market breaking, not just cooling

breakeven_10y.note: Market-implied inflation. Watch DIRECTION: a sharp rise alongside rising real yields means the bond market is repricing inflation AND the term premium.

real_yield_10y.note: No single danger level. Real yields >2.5% historically squeeze equity multiples and EM; the rate of change matters more than the level.

fed_balance_sheet.note: Direction, not level: balance-sheet shrinkage drains liquidity (QT); expansion adds it. Read together with RRP.

risk_thresholds._new_band_disclosure: Bands for the Europe/UK/Asia/EM indicators are the analyst's proposed starting thresholds (historical-stress calibrated), not official limits — adjust to your own view.

my_cpi_yoy.danger: >5% — well outside Malaysia's recent range; subsidy rationalisation / ringgit pass-through risk

myr_3m_move.danger: >5% depreciation in 3M — capital-outflow / risk-off signal (positive = ringgit weaker)

my_opr.note: Policy rate — direction matters, not level. A cut signals growth worry; a hike signals inflation/ringgit defence.

usd_myr.note: Level alone has no fixed danger line; use the 3-month move card for stress.

klci.note: Equity index: no fixed band. Use the history context rather than a threshold.

brent.note: Two-sided for Malaysia: oil and gas feed Petronas dividends and government revenue (low oil hurts the fiscal side), while high oil raises subsidy cost and inflation.

palm_oil.note: Plantation and export-earnings driver; falling prices hit plantation earnings and ringgit sentiment. No fixed band.

real_economy_stress._purpose: The financial-market indicators above (JGB, USDJPY, BOJ rate) don't show the political constraint on how far BOJ can hike or how long yen weakness can be tolerated. This section tracks that constraint directly: how currency weakness + inflation are showing up as real corporate failures, which is the pressure limiting policy options.

corporate_bankruptcies_h1_2026.note: Two independent credit research firms (Tokyo Shoko Research and Teikoku Databank), close but not identical counts — normal given differing methodology. Both confirm: first time above 5,000 in H1 in 12 years (since 2014's 5,073 by TSR's count).

monthly.note: TSR headline confirms June crossed 1,000 for first time in 2 years 1 month; exact monthly digits sourced from a TV broadcast graphic, not independently re-verified against TSR's monthly release.

labor_shortage_related.note: record high for a first half

of_which_wage_cost_surge.note: TSR: 賃上げが重荷に — wage increases becoming a bankruptcy driver, confirmed

price_hike_type.note: sourced from TV graphic, directionally consistent with TSR's 物価高倒産 category but not independently re-verified digit-by-digit

sme_concentration.note: sourced from TV graphic — plausible given TSR's own H1 report shows 77% of all bankruptcies have liabilities under ¥100mn, i.e. concentrated in small/micro firms, though the exact 90.6% employee-count cut wasn't independently found in the TSR/TDB source documents reviewed

corporate_bankruptcies_h1_2026.source: Tokyo Shoko Research (tsr-net.co.jp), Teikoku Databank (tdb.co.jp), both published 2026-07-08

ppi_import_price_passthrough.cgpi_trend: Feb +2.1% -> Mar +2.8% -> Apr +5.3% -> May +6.3% -> Jun +7.3% -> Jul +7.2% (second straight month above 7%, first time above 7% since around 2023)
ppi_import_price_passthrough.note: BOJ's own data (published 2026-08-13). This is the real-economy transmission channel for a weak yen: import costs -> corporate input costs -> either passed to consumers (inflation) or absorbed (margin/bankruptcy pressure) — both outcomes visible in the bankruptcy-by-cause data above.
ppi_import_price_passthrough.source: Bank of Japan CGPI release, Nikkei, 2026-08-13

curry_price_index_tdb._purpose: Teikoku Databank's household-cost-of-living proxy — tracks cost to cook curry rice at home, updated monthly, faster and more visceral than headline CPI.
curry_price_index_tdb.note: 370 yen in Jan 2026 was a record high on the post-2026-rebase methodology. Series underwent a base-year revision in 2026 — pre-2026 figures (e.g. 2025 readings in the 390s-400s) are NOT directly comparable to 2026 figures on a like-for-like basis. Treat this as a directional/momentum indicator, not a clean YoY series, until both sides of the rebase are reconciled.
curry_price_index_tdb.source: Teikoku Databank monthly カレーライス物価指数 releases, tdb.co.jp

central_bank_calendar._purpose: Remaining scheduled meetings for 2026, sourced directly from each central bank's own published calendar (not aggregators). Add new dates here once each bank publishes its 2027 schedule.

media_fact_checks._purpose: Claims sourced from a TV news graphic (2026-08-15) that were checked against primary sources — most held up; two didn't and are flagged rather than silently corrected.
checked_and_accurate: Curry price index ~370 yen Jan 2026 record high

flagged_as_overstated.issue: The YoY growth RATE was higher as recently as Dec 2022 (~+10.6%) during the post-Ukraine energy shock. 7.2% is a genuine 2-year-high and the 2nd straight month above 7%, but not the highest print in living memory — the '44-year' framing looks like broadcast-headline embellishment, not an official BOJ characterization.

flagged_as_overstated.claim: Japan holds '1.4 trillion USD' in US Treasuries
flagged_as_overstated.issue: Official US Treasury TIC data shows Japan's holdings around $1.14-1.23tn through mid-2026 (e.g. $1,225.3bn Jan 2026, $1,143.1bn May 2026) — real, still the largest foreign holder, but roughly $150-250bn below the figure quoted.

china_property._purpose: China property/LGFV is the slow-burn channel: it hits global growth via commodities and banks, not via a daily price. No free daily API exists, so this is a CHECKLIST to verify against primary releases, not a live number.
china_property.status: NOT YET VERIFIED — values intentionally left blank rather than guessed

check_monthly.primary_source: National Bureau of Statistics of China (stats.gov.cn) monthly release
check_monthly.why: Sustained m/m declines = collateral erosion for banks and LGFVs

check_monthly.item: Property investment y/y and new starts
check_monthly.why: Leading indicator for steel, copper, iron ore demand

check_monthly.item: Developer distress (Vanke and other large developers): bond extensions, defaults
check_monthly.why: Contagion to banks and trust products

check_monthly.primary_source: PBoC / MoF statements; Wind/Bloomberg if available

china_property.danger_triggers: Disorderly developer default affecting a state-linked entity; broad CNY depreciation >5% in 3M (see CNY card); policy-bank rescue announcements.

taiwan_watch._purpose: Taiwan is a supply-chain single point of failure (advanced semiconductors). It is a tail-risk tag, not a forecast, and has no price signal until it is too late.
taiwan_watch.status: NOT YET VERIFIED — qualitative tag; update from primary sources

indicators_to_watch.primary_source: Taiwan Ministry of National Defense daily reports (mnd.gov.tw)

indicators_to_watch.item: Large named exercises / live-fire closure areas
indicators_to_watch.primary_source: PLA Eastern Theater Command announcements; Taiwan MND

indicators_to_watch.item: TWD and KOSPI/TAIEX stress (see TWD and KRW cards)

taiwan_watch.escalation_ladder: 1) Elevated drills (routine) -> 2) Named exercise with blockade rehearsal -> 3) Quarantine/inspection regime -> 4) Kinetic. Markets typically price only from step 3; TWD and semiconductor equities move first.

malaysia_watch._purpose: Malaysian indicators with no free reliable daily feed. This is a verify-against-primary-source checklist. No numbers here are claimed; click through for the current figure.
malaysia_watch.status: NOT AUTO-UPDATED — open the official source for the live figure
malaysia_watch.next_mpc: BNM's next Monetary Policy Committee meeting is in November 2026 per press reports; confirm the exact date on BNM's official MPC calendar.

items.why: Sovereign funding cost; the key Malaysia-specific rates signal
Buffer against ringgit and outflow stress

items.item: Fiscal deficit and federal debt vs statutory limit (MOF Fiscal Outlook / Budget)
Foreign flows into Malaysian bonds and equities (BNM / Bursa)
items.why: Ringgit pressure shows up in flows before price

items.item: Household debt and bank asset quality (BNM Financial Stability Review)
